question: Which of the following compounds is NOT formed when ferrous sulphate is heated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphuric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When ferrous sulphate (FeSO₄) is heated, it undergoes thermal decomposition to form ferric oxide (Fe₂O₃), sulphur dioxide (SO₂), and sulphur trioxide (SO₃).
 
• Ferrous sulphate decomposes in the following manner:

 2 FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃
 
• Sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) is not formed in this reaction.
 
• The decomposition typically occurs at temperatures between 480°C and 500°C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO₄):**

 
 
• It is a green crystalline solid.
 
• It is used in various applications such as water treatment, and as a precursor to other iron compounds.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Decomposition:**
 
 
• It is a chemical decomposition caused by heat.
 
• It involves breaking down compounds into simpler substances when heated.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂):**
 
 
• It is a toxic gas with a pungent, irritating smell.
 
• It is used as a preservative and in the production of sulphuric acid.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur Trioxide (SO₃):**
 
 
• It is a chemical compound that is used in the production of sulphuric acid.
 
• It is highly reactive and can cause severe burns on contact.
